necessary_context.content: Each entry of Omega is independent N(0,1). Theorem 10.5 concerns fixed real A in R^{m x n}, integer k>=2 and p>=2 with ell=k+p<=min(m,n). Algorithm 4.1 itself takes a sample count ell; the k,p restrictions belong to its selected performance regime.
necessary_context.name: Gaussian sketch and selected real regime

necessary_context.content: P_M is the unique orthogonal projector onto range(M); * denotes transpose in the selected real case. For an orthonormal basis Q of range(Y), QQ*=P_Y. Frobenius norm squared is the sum of squared matrix entries. Singular values are ordered nonincreasingly; the tail sum ends at min(m,n).
necessary_context.name: Projection and norms

necessary_context.content: In SVD coordinates Omega_1=V_1*Omega and Omega_2=V_2*Omega, with V_1 containing the first k right singular vectors. Theorem 9.1, under full row rank of Omega_1, bounds the squared Frobenius residual by ||Sigma_2||_F^2+||Sigma_2 Omega_2 Omega_1^dagger||_F^2. Proposition 10.1 Eq.(10.1) gives E||SGT||_F^2=||S||_F^2||T||_F^2 for fixed compatible S,T and standard Gaussian G. Proposition 10.2 Eq.(10.3) gives E||G^dagger||_F^2=k/(p-1) for k x (k+p) standard Gaussian G, k,p>=2.
necessary_context.name: Source Proof dependencies

necessary_context.content: Algorithm 4.1 returns a basis. Forming B=Q*A and a direct SVD is Stage B. §5.1 charges the dense product separately, and p.30 notes use of A* products. Remark 5.1 distinguishes subsequent rank-k truncation from the approximation with the full basis.
necessary_context.name: Stage B is separately charged
